Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: GIMTEL (national switch) is constituted “under the aegis” of the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie (BCM) ([GIMTEL](https://gimtel.mr/fr/missions)). BCM is also a member of GIMTEL, and BCM’s Governor participated in the launch of an interoperable mobile payment project implemented by GIMTEL ([GBM Banque](https://www.gbm-banque.com/en/actualites/bcm-new-agreement-implementation-interoperable-mobile-payment-project)). This indicates central bank involvement beyond regulation, with governance/oversight and participation in the scheme.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Mauritania has an operational national payments switch (GIMTEL) that connects banks/ATMs/POS and supports interoperable electronic/card payments and real-time settlement ([TransFi](https://www.transfi.com/blog/mauritanias-payment-rails-how-they-work---national-switch-e-banking-mobile-wallet-expansion)). GIMTEL’s mission is to create an interbank Mauritanian platform for payment and cash withdrawal and to implement required technical infrastructure ([GIMTEL](https://gimtel.mr/fr/missions)). A 2025 tender sought “implementation of an instant payment system in Mauritania enabling interoperability of financial services”, suggesting further IPS buildout beyond existing rails ([MauritaniaTenders](https://www.mauritaniatenders.com/tender/implementation-instant-payment-system-mauritania-enabling-interoperability-financial-services-7034e4b.php)).

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Global Findex figures cited by UNCDF indicate mobile money account ownership was about 4% of adults in 2018, which is <20% ([UNCDF Policy Accelerator](https://policyaccelerator.uncdf.org/whats-new/mauritania-regulatory-framework)). No newer nationally representative active-user share was located, so the score reflects the latest cited penetration evidence.
